title: Thoryn provisioning file (.thoryn/provision.yaml)
description: SSO-3088 (epic SSO-3087) — the DESIRED STATE of a repository's Thoryn resources, converged idempotently by `thoryn provision plan | apply | destroy`. Resources, not steps: each has a stable `name` the CLI uses as its converge key. The `kind` values form a CLOSED allowlist mapping only to supported product APIs (the product-boundary rule made structural). Secrets NEVER enter this file: a key that carries a secret value is rejected; name the ENV VAR that carries it instead (`passwordEnv`, `smtpPasswordEnv`, `clientSecretEnv`).

kind.description: CLOSED allowlist of resource kinds, each mapping to one supported product API. `emailProvider`, `loginTheme`, `loginFlow` and `loginMethods` are singletons per environment (no `name` needed). `loginMethods` (SSO-3100) is the sign-in METHOD allow-list the hosted login offers (`PUT /api/v1/login-methods`; `destroy` resets it to the default via `DELETE`). `user` exists so a scenario can declare its test account; a customer's real users self-register. `customDomain` (SSO-3413) is the workspace's ONE custom domain (`/api/v1/custom-domain`): workspace-level (no `environment`) and a singleton (no `name` needed). `plan` shows the DNS records to publish, `apply` claims `spec.host` and verifies it, and only `--prune` / `destroy` with `--confirm <workspace-slug>` release it. The signed-in identity needs `tenant:domains.*` and, unless it is a workspace admin, an explicit grant (`thoryn access grant client:<id> manager custom_domain:<workspace-id>`). `workloadIdentityTrust` (SSO-3689; ADR 2026-10-14 credential ladder) is a workload-identity TRUST of the resource's environment (`/api/v1/workload-identity/trusts`): the identity a CI job or a pod presents instead of a secret, by `provider` (`github_actions` | `forgejo` | `kubernetes`) with that provider's pins. Converged by `name`; the hub's pins are IMMUTABLE, so a declared field that differs from the live trust is the plan error `workload_identity_trust_immutable` (delete and re-create, or declare what is live). An `application` binds one by NAME through `spec.federatedTrust`. The identity applying a file cannot declare its OWN bootstrap trust (chicken-and-egg): that first trust is created once by a person; everything else is declared.

name.description: Stable converge key (unique per kind within the file). Required for every non-singleton kind.

environment.description: The environment this resource lives in: the `name` of an `environment` resource in this file, or the slug of an environment that already exists. May be a `{{env.NAME}}` placeholder, resolved from the environment when the file is read (an unset variable is an error). Omitted ⇒ the workspace's production plane. Not allowed on an `environment` resource.

spec.description: Kind-specific desired state, forwarded to the product API. Property names ending in password / secret / token are REJECTED — use `<key>Env` naming the env var that carries the value.

readOnly.description: SSO-3659 (ADR 2026-10-13 §1) — `true` declares that this repository DEPENDS ON the resource and does not own it. `plan` / `apply` look it up live and require it to MATCH the declared spec: any field difference is the plan error `access_read_only` (non-zero exit; `apply` refuses before writing anything). A read-only reference is never created, adopted, recorded in the receipt, or removed, and `viewer` reach on it suffices (an OWNED resource — the default — needs `manager`, held directly or inherited from its environment / workspace; see `thoryn access`). It cannot carry `grants`. `thoryn provision import` renders a resource the repository may only view this way.

publishTo.description: SSO-3668 (ADR 2026-10-13 production-clients-declared-in-the-config-project §2) — where `apply` PUBLISHES this resource's id once it is converged. `application` only: the clientId is the one output a resource has, and it is public by construction (it appears in every authorization URL) — so a target is always a VARIABLE, never a secret. Published on EVERY apply (an upsert, so a re-created client propagates without a second step), AFTER the resource is converged and recorded in the receipt. A target the signed-in credential cannot reach is the apply error `publish_target_unreachable`: the client exists, the receipt records its id, and the error names the one `gh variable set` a human can run. `plan` prints the pending publish as a line. Refused on a `readOnly` reference (it publishes nothing — the owning repository publishes). The receipt records what was published (kind, repository, environment, name).

kind.description: `githubActionsVariable`: an Actions variable on a GitHub repository's environment, upserted with `gh variable set <name> --body <clientId> --repo <repository> --env <environment>` (the environment is created when absent; an existing environment's protection is never touched).

repository.description: The target repository as `owner/name` (for a production client: the application repository the config project publishes to).

environment.description: The target repository's GitHub environment (e.g. `production`); only a job targeting it reads the variable.

name.description: The Actions variable name, e.g. `THORYN_PRODUCTION_CLIENT_ID`. GitHub reserves the `GITHUB_` prefix.

secretSink.description: SSO-3659 (ADR 2026-10-13 converge §5 — secrets are delivered where they are consumed, never into a CI secret store; production-clients ADR §3 tier 3) — WHERE `apply` DELIVERS the one-time `client_secret` a confidential `application` is minted with, the moment the client is converged and recorded in the receipt. `kubernetesSecret`: `data.<key>` of the Kubernetes Secret `<namespace>/<name>`, written through your own `kubectl` (`kubectl -n <namespace> create secret generic <name> --from-file=<key>=/dev/stdin --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -` — the value rides on stdin, never on argv; the namespace must already exist, it is never created). `file`: an owner-only (`0600`) file at `path`, never overwritten unless `apply --force`. The secret itself never enters this file, the plan, the receipt or a log. A target that cannot be reached is the apply error `undelivered_secrets`: the client exists, the receipt records it, the exit is non-zero, and the recovery is `thoryn clients rotate-secret <clientId> --secret-file <path>`. `plan` prints the intended delivery as a line (no secret exists at plan time). Only on `kind: application`, only when the client is confidential (`clientType: public` is minted nothing), and never on a `readOnly` reference. Omitted ⇒ the CLI's `--secret-file` / interactive-TTY channel.

namespace.description: An EXISTING Kubernetes namespace (RFC 1123 label); thoryn never creates one.

path.description: The owner-only (`0600`) file the secret is written to; an existing file is not overwritten unless `apply --force`.

grants.description: SSO-3113 (epic SSO-3108) — least-privilege ACCESS GRANTS on this resource, converged with it by `apply`: a listed grant that is missing is created, a grant on this object the file no longer lists is revoked (the workspace admin userset `workspace:<id>#admin` is never revoked; grants on objects the file does not own are never touched). The OBJECT is implicit — it derives from the receipt id (`environment:<id>`, `application:<clientId>`, `user:<id>`, `federation_member:<id>`, `<singleton>:<envSlug>`, `custom_domain:<workspace-id>`). Omit to leave the object's grants unmanaged; `[]` declares none. Needs `tenant:access.write` (a session without it fails closed).

relation.description: `manager` or `viewer`. SSO-3673: `owner` is a platform relation (one owning repository per application / environment) but is NOT accepted here — a repository cannot claim ownership by writing YAML; a workspace admin grants it with `thoryn access grant <subject> owner <object>`.

slug.description: A slug, or a `{{env.NAME}}` placeholder resolved from the environment at apply time (a per-run sandbox in CI).

clientAuthenticationMethods.description: SSO-3689 (ADR 2026-10-14 credential ladder) — how the client authenticates at the token endpoint, as the hub's method tokens: `private_key_jwt` (rung 1: the app's own key pair; `jwksUri` or inline `jwks` REQUIRED), `federated_assertion` (rung 2: the workload's platform identity token is the client assertion; ALWAYS the only method, `federatedTrust` REQUIRED, no key, no secret, `authorization_code` / `refresh_token` only, PKCE stays required, never `clientType: public`), `client_secret_basic` (a Thoryn-minted secret; the only method a `secretSink:` is legal with), `none` (a public client). `client_secret_post` is deliberately NOT declarable: a secret in the request body is the courier rung. Omitted ⇒ product-api's default for the `clientType` (`client_secret_basic` for confidential, `none` for public). Converged on UPDATE together with `jwksUri` / `jwks` / `federatedTrust`.

jwksUri.description: Where the client's PUBLIC keys are fetched for `private_key_jwt` (HTTPS). Exactly one of `jwksUri` and `jwks`. The API does not render the key location, so the receipt records what this file last applied and a change converges from that.

jwks.description: The client's PUBLIC JWK Set for `private_key_jwt`, inline (`{ keys: [ { kty, kid, … } ] }`): RSA / EC keys with a `kid`, NO private parameters (`d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`, `oth`, `k` are refused). Exactly one of `jwksUri` and `jwks`.

federatedTrust.description: SSO-3689 (ADR 2026-10-14 federated client authentication §11) — the NAME of a `workloadIdentityTrust` in the SAME environment (declared in this file, or one that already exists); the engine resolves it to the trust id before the create / update, and the API takes the id. Required with `federated_assertion`, refused without it (`federated_trust_without_method`); a missing or other-environment trust is the plan error `federated_trust_not_found`.

methods.description: The FULL sign-in method allow-list, in display order (e.g. password, magic_link, magic_code, passkey, totp, sms); the server rejects an unknown token. Converged as a SET (order-insensitive).

host.description: The host to claim: a subdomain you control, e.g. `auth.acme.com` (the platform refuses apex domains, IP addresses and Thoryn domains).

acceptReSignIn.description: Required `true` when the workspace already has production users: a custom domain changes the workspace's issuer, so every production user signs in again once. Recorded on the claim and in the audit log.

provider.description: The workload's platform: `github_actions` (pin block `github`), `forgejo` (pin block `forgejo`) or `kubernetes` (pin block `kubernetes`). Exactly the provider's block is present.

scopes.description: The `tenant:` scopes a job / pod may obtain with this trust — a CEILING: the hub refuses a scope the applying identity does not itself hold (`403 scope_not_grantable`), so a trust can never widen the reach of the identity that declares it. Converged as a set.

confirmProduction.description: Required `true` for a trust on the PRODUCTION plane (no `environment`, or the `production` slug): its jobs / pods then act on production. The hub refuses without it (`production_confirmation_required`). Create-time only; never diffed.

github.description: `github_actions` pins: `repository` as `owner/name`; `ownerId` + `repositoryId` (GitHub's immutable ids — both or neither; required for a private repository, looked up once for a public one); `environment` (the GitHub environment the job must run in — REQUIRED for a production trust); `ref` (exact, e.g. `refs/heads/main`); `githubHostedRunnersOnly`.

forgejo.description: `forgejo` pins: `instanceUrl` (the instance origin, `https://host`, no path); `owner` + `ownerId` and `repository` + `repositoryId` (the instance's immutable ids — REQUIRED, a Forgejo instance may be private); `ref` (exact — REQUIRED for a production trust: Forgejo has no environments).

kubernetes.description: `kubernetes` pins (SSO-3678, rung 3): `issuer` (the cluster's exact OIDC issuer, `https://…`); `namespace` and `serviceAccount` (REQUIRED for a production trust; `serviceAccount` needs `namespace`); `jwks` — the cluster's PUBLIC JWK Set (`kubectl get --raw /openid/v1/jwks`), pinned inline for a cluster whose issuer Thoryn cannot reach: RSA / EC keys with a `kid`, NO private parameters. Without `jwks` Thoryn discovers the keys from the issuer.
